opening.quote: Good morning, Tidewell homes, my name his Lotte. How can I help?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name in your first turn, which meets the opening standard.

verification.quote: Name and order number or postcode.
verification.comment: You asked for verification but the caller gave only a first name and order number, and you never confirmed the full name before sharing order details; ask for the full name and confirm it against the order.

understanding.quote: Okay, Siobhan. Chair, a €95.00, delivered days ago. You want to return it because you don't like it?
understanding.comment: You captured the return request and confirmed the reason, though you did not check the delivery date precisely before answering.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Our return window is 30 days from uh delivery, so I can't accept return now.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The 30-day window is correct, but the caller said the chair was held for 6 weeks, which is past 30 days, so the stated refusal is right; however you should have confirmed the delivery date before stating it, and you promised nothing wrong, so this is accurate.

process_compliance.quote: Those our the I'll e-mail you this information today. Anything else?
process_compliance.comment: No hold was used, so no hold step applied; the call did not involve damage, bank disputes or vouchers, so no required step was missed.

communication.comment: The caller expressed disappointment and you did not acknowledge it; respond with empathy such as saying you understand the disappointment before moving on.

closing.quote: tank you for calling titwell. Goodbye.
closing.comment: You asked if there was anything else and thanked the caller, but you did not clearly confirm what happens next, since the email content was vague; state exactly what the email will contain.
